Seeing the joy among the Nāgas, a beautiful Nāga maiden herself appeared, as if born from the desire of Śambhu to create a wife for him.
The enjoyer. || 764 ||

She who, by means of the appropriate and supreme absorption into the self-portion, causes all that is moving and unmoving— which rests upon dissolution— to be disjoined from it, she moves along the path of the serpent.
She who is called "possessing enjoyment" is [also] "deprived of union. || 64 ||
p. 259) She who is dear to enjoyment. || 765 ||
Even though she is one, if she manifests the duality of the enjoyer, the enjoyed, and so forth,
then for that very reason, I know her to be eternally fond of enjoyment.
Knowledge encompasses all treatises. || 766 ||
May this faultless knowledge, containing all the scriptures, which is delightful through its great clarity in both prose and verse, always reside in the heart for the sake of awakening.
Excellent memory. || 767 ||
How could all [beings] not remember with one-pointed mind that pair of lotus-feet, by which excellent memory itself is well-remembered? (67)
She who speaks the Dharma. || 768 ||
She who commands the Dharma in manifold ways, yet does not herself deviate from the manifold dharmas, nor from the singular Dharma—she is truly a speaker of the Dharma. (68)
The Veda. || 769 ||
That scripture which has the witness as its object attains the state of being the universal subject;
this particular Śruti is like Brahmā himself, the Mother of the World. 69.
Those who possess the power of retaining what they have heard. || 770 ||
Since at the beginning of creation, Druhiṇa and the other gods receive all the Śruti for the sake of the world's activity,
she is the supreme one who spontaneously upholds the Śruti.
Jyeṣṭhā || 771 ||
Even those most eminent and venerable sages headed by Vasiṣṭha, renowned throughout the three worlds, having completed their studies, received from her the primordial instruction. (p. 260)
The eldest is Vasiṣṭhā; she alone is always present. || 71 ||
The most excellent. || 772 ||
She is unseen by those who have not perceived the Dharma, yet seen by the wise;
she is the destruction and nourishment of the base and the wicked,
established in her own essential unity, and satisfied by her own devotion.
But she is our most excellent, most steadfast one who accomplishes our own desires. || 72 ||
Dwelling in the netherworld (pātālavāsinī). || 773 ||
Having blocked all other paths by her three strides, does she who causes devotion to blossom not abide in the netherworld for the supreme satisfaction of Bali? (73)
Investigation || 774 ||
Alas, the Veda— whose manifold meanings are difficult to comprehend due to figurative expressions, which is the sole cause of misconception, and which resembles the ocean by serving as a bridge—
is here properly bound together by her who, through the grace of the True One, instantly effects the enumeration of the Vedas for all.
May this Mīmāṃsā bestow upon us the play of speech that resounds through the treatises of the wise. || 74 ||
The science of logic. || 775 ||
By means of the sixteen-fold determination of objects, the knower attains the supreme good; and by that same [means], he here reveals the pure word for the sake of others.
That science of logic is known to be faultless. || 75 ||
p. 261) Subhaktiḥ || 776 ||
Even after performing the most arduous penances and having studied all four Vedas,
a person who lacks mental discipline attains nothing at all.
Until such time as true devotion is remembered by the wise one. || 76 ||
She who is affectionate toward her devotees. || 777 ||
Even one of low birth and an ill-favored body, if devoted and free from deceit, attains honor from kings; clearly, she is affectionate toward her devotees. (77)
One with a beautiful navel. || 778 ||
Even the Supreme Lord is perpetually submerged in her navel, which takes the form of a whirlpool in the ocean of the King of Essences, whose waves are nectar.
May this [girdle] with its beautiful navel be my protector. || 78 ||
Torment || 779 ||
If there exists a nourishment even for torment, then let that nourishment for everyone be the state of Śiva, brought about precisely by the poverty of illusion and its effects within me. (79)
How could that which has a single locus determine multiple individuals?
For there would be no universal whatsoever that could bring about the cognition of both unity and multiplicity. (80)
Profound. || 781 ||
If the all-knowing consciousness did not exist, who would keep their own respective secrets hidden? (p.
262) The steady ones [attain] the activity of the circle of the lords of heroes.
It should be profound, self-luminous, and free from expectations. || 81 ||
Devoid of existence. || 782 ||
She who, though fond of worldly existence, contemplates even non-existence as existence;
though her nature is existence, she is, alas, by her very essence devoid of existence. 82.
The form is the bearer of the serpent-noose. || 783 ||
In the peril of battle, may that form which holds the serpent-noose, and by its play destroyed the army of the wicked enemy—the lord of serpents—be ever present. 83.
Unfathomable. || 784 ||
Even the Three-eyed Lord, though his own calamities have been destroyed,
is never able to determine what the nature of that [form] is, nor how much of it there is, even to this day.
Or rather, she is not Bhavānī, for she is not unfathomable. 84.
Nāgakuṇḍalā || 785 ||
With the radiance of her ears and beautiful cheeks joined by spotless locks of hair, she, adorned with golden earrings, shines like a serpent wearing jeweled earrings. 85.
Sucakrā || 786 ||

May she who is worshipped by the lords of the wheels (*cakreśvara*) within the wheel of perfect emptiness—she who destroys crookedness even in those faces that are curved by the many pure patterns of the wheels—be a perfectly auspicious wheel for us on all sides. (86)
She stands in the center of the wheel. || 787 ||

Marked by the status of the leader of the assembly of gods, asuras, and chief apsarases, this auspicious goddess, holding a discus in her hand and standing in the very center of the wheel, is victorious. 87.
She dwells in the corner of the wheel. (788)
How could he who has constantly served her, the one dwelling in the corner of the wheel, not surely attain the vast state of a universal monarch? 88.
The Vidyā consists of all mantras. || 789 ||
The supreme knowledge to be known by those who know the mantras, the cause of the expansion of the Vedas, consisting of all mantras—may this Vidyā be perfected within my heart this very day. 89.
The row of syllables of all mantras. || 790 ||
This unprecedented, supreme secret is the extinction of unabated pride;
she alone exists everywhere as the entire sequence of all mantra-syllables. (90)
Madhusravā || 791 ||
May this Madhumatī river— whose sweetness and fragrance entice the bees, which was the former playground of the splendor of spring,
and which is frequented by those rich in honey— grant success upon her banks that are resonant with honey.
Flowing forth. || 792 ||
Even though it is produced from harsh wood, the grape is a manifest elixir;
that it nevertheless expands [its sweetness] is surely some mysterious law of nature arising from its proximity to a flowing river.
Bhrāmarī || 793 ||

Though worthy of universal sovereignty and equal to the Lord of Beings (Śiva), Rāma wandered for as many years as there are marks on the body of the earth, his heart agitated by the pain of separation.
That [power] is Bhrāmarī; cause our evil delusion to revolve away.
The *bhramarālakā* [metre] consists of [the following pattern]: || 794 ||
That young girl with bee-like curls is fully capable of destroying the impurity of his lotus-face, whose beauty is shimmering like a row of bees. 94.
She stands in the center of the circle of mothers. || 795 ||
Praised by the bearer of the maṇḍala and by the bearer of the water-pot, may she who stands in the midst of the circle of Mothers grant us the state of being the Lord of the Maṇḍala. 95.
She who dwells within the circle of the Mothers. || 796 ||
Having taken leave of those best of gods who had come to the assembly in the morning, one woman alone, dwelling within the circle of her mothers, continues to enjoy herself. 96.
The mother of the prince. || 797 ||
She who alone acts like a maiden is the ground of doubt regarding the realm of Māra’s enemies;
she is that young girl, the mother of Kumāra, whose sole bond is the reckoning of Māra as Time.
O cruel one, make the sound "ka-ka-ka-ka," making a hand that sounds like "kakakāra" with every stroke; O you who possess the form of the full moon's rays, bring the doer of deeds into your hand! 98.
This two-syllable [mantra] is Sumukhī. || 799 ||
He possesses a natural beauty enhanced by excellent forest ornaments made of flowers, guñjā berries, and the like, which rests upon the power of his loveliness.
That auspicious one, whose face is gracious, is the foremost [of all] as "Sumukhī" (the Fair-faced One).
The destroyer of fever. || 800 ||
Since the chronic fever of existence is cured by the beautiful-eyed one alone, even without the treatment of a skilled physician or the performance of many mantras, yantras, and rituals.
It is said that she, Lalitā, is the destroyer of fever. || 100 ||
When the poem of that one known as Sāhib Kaula— so called because he has established his seat by means of the power of experiencing the supreme freedom of his own self—
has arrived, his sister, who provides the illustrative examples, has become ready.
In this world, devotion reached its culmination in the thirteenth [chapter] titled "The Cessation of the Play of Citrānta. (101)
Thus ends the thirteenth devotion in the *Nāmavilāsa*, composed by the illustrious and preeminent teacher of Mahāmāheśvara, Sāhib Kaulānandanātha. 13.
The fourteenth devotion has passed. 801.

If those past non-Buddhist disputants were indeed wise, why was it that they did not know [the truth] when they stood before me as a disputant? Or rather, if they were wise, why did they not speak out? Or perhaps they were not wise at all. (1)
(This is the half-rotation. This is its placement:
a, tī.
Those indeed are the days.
To you,
O Light.
To the non-Buddhists.
In heaven, in heaven.
The radiance has shone forth.
When he gives to us.
Do not [speak] thus.
or to him, indeed.
I do not know.
Do not be afraid.
Existing. || 802 ||
Whether in the present, the past, or the future, may she alone—who is truly existent, faultless, pure, and heart-pleasing—be gracious this very moment. (2)
[This is indeed the fourth] future one. || 803 ||
O Bhavānī, through our experience of the power of the inseparable connection between existence and non-existence,
may you be present in every new and ever-renewing birth within the forest of worldly existence.
This three-syllabled [mantra] is Prītimañjarī. || 804 ||
May that very bud of affection also blossom within you as it has within me,
by which even the unpleasant becomes pleasant, and through various means, even the most disagreeable becomes agreeable.
The method for possessing all happiness. || 805 ||
The mind does not shine anywhere for anyone without her;
this very logic, which possesses all happiness, is victorious, O wise one! (5)
It transforms the food. || 806 ||
That single [power] which manifests the sixfold state in various forms is praised by the knowers of truth as the "transformer of food" (āhārapariṇāminī).
The causal basis of the five elements. || 807 ||
By which even insentient beings are set in motion toward their objects;
that power of primordial nature (prakṛti), the cause of the five elements, is victorious.
She who carries one across the ocean of existence. || 808 ||

She who carries one across the ocean of existence, she who carries one across the ocean of existence; O Bhava, she who carries one across the ocean of existence, she who carries one across the ocean of existence. || 8 ||
[All-foot-yaṃaka] (p. 268): Akrūra || 809 ||
Upon merely beholding her, even a most wicked person momentarily abandons his own nature— whether by reeling or otherwise— and thus this gentle lady holds sovereignty over the mind.
Grahavatī || 810 ||
Wherever these planets manifest, she is not touched by them at all;
like the sky alone, she is victorious—though surrounded by planets, she remains free from their grasp.
[This is not the fourth:
the dismemberments. || 811 ||

Victorious is that Goddess of Planets (Graheśvarī), who gathers those who have accumulated the results of their actions; she is free from fear toward those difficult to subdue, yet she thoroughly restrains them; she is embraced by Fortune, and her very form is victory itself.
Free from the planets. || 812 ||
It is not surprising that one whose heart is purified by devotion to Him cannot be touched even in a dream by the planets;
for the Goddess herself is likewise free from the influence of the planets.
Rohiṇī || 813 ||

Resplendent as the crest-jewel of the lover of Rohiṇī, the ascending ladder for travelers on the path to the abode of liberation, worshipped by the son of Rohiṇī, unconquered, and absolute—victorious is that very Rohiṇī! 13.
The Earth-womb. || 814 ||
Having attained liberation from dwelling in the womb, that seed reaches a state of fruition never before seen;
she alone is expert in the single moment of the composition of manifold forms.
That bold woman, whose womb is the earth, is victorious. || 14 ||
The ground of time. || 815 ||
Even Time, having pervaded her,
does not suddenly become the "Time of Death" (Kālakāla) for one who possesses devotion to her and whose palm tree of virtue is exceedingly vast.
She is the ground of time, ever-playful with the arts of childhood and the like. || 15 ||
She who abides in time. || 816 ||
Time never oversteps that which it has reached, just as a shadow does not pass beyond its own head;
since she too exists within time, who could exist outside of it? (16)
A woman who is devoid of blemish. || 817 ||
Neither a celestial woman, nor an asura woman, nor any other woman radiant with grace captivates the mind as this blemishless lady does. (17)
It runs toward the sixty-four [directions]. || 818 ||
For the attainment of the fruits of the four aims of life, she who is praised by the mouth of the Four-faced One (Brahmā) is renowned in the four directions and flows through sixty-four names.
Worn out. || 819 ||
For Vṛkodara, though born of the Wind and a son of Pāṇḍu,
digested through his meditative power food that was joined with a human body and beyond the comprehension of others.
May this [herb], though itself decayed, dispel my undigested illness. || 19 ||
Wearing tattered clothes. || 820 ||
This is the propriety of a devoted wife: that even toward her husband who was clothed only by the directions, she remained ever-new by wearing worn-out garments in order to comply with him.
The new one. || 821 ||
The mind, whose function has reached its limit through experience, knows and perceives the states of its exceedingly aged grandfather and others,
even though it has transcended the six states; this remains a marvel even today.
That Bhavānī is indeed ever-new as the mother of the worlds.
The new beloved. || 822 ||

Because of the attainment of this [goddess], even the Lord of the Supreme, the enemy of Smara, though he was a mere pillar (sthāṇu) impaled on a spike, became the conqueror of Death; victorious is this Navavallabhā of Śaṅkara! 22.
Free from dust. || 823 ||
The enemy of the king of kings of kings, who has conquered kingdoms and conquered old age;
who wears away passion, whose vigor is undiminished, who is the king of kings, who is free from decay, and who is stainless.
This [consists of] two syllables:
"O Narmadā, you are indeed distinguished everywhere; here, however, your delight is supreme.
For, having been seized by a portion of her, Viṣṇu abandoned Lakṣmī on his own chest, while the Lord of the Universe made your daughter’s speech dwell within his own tongue."
Or even a king with his retinue is formidable, yet the mountain is incomparably more so.
(This is the *cakrabandha*); its placement is joy. || 825 ||

Whatever [poetic composition] composed by another steals away one's own distinct nature; whatever supreme [meditation], when meditated upon with a single mental faculty, causes one to forget all other arts;
and whatever [speech] is like the earth that draws up every essence and destroys ill-seeing—[may she grant us grace].
May there be love for us from everyone here, with every part [of their being], everywhere, and at all times. 25.
It increases passion and attachment. || 826 ||
Increasing passion and delight,
Lalitā plays gracefully before Yama, caressing him in all the arts; she who is pure and exceedingly playful makes everything fruitful.
The Lalanas never carry him away; it is a wonder! || 26 ||
The fivefold course of the wind is divided. || 827 ||
If the fivefold movement of the winds, which reside within a single body and possess the unique skill of their respective functions, remains distinct yet non-distinct, then there is no fear.
The earth consists of five reservoirs of phlegm.
May this earth, whose pure surface is rendered confident by the delight in the flavors of food and drink,
remove the diseases of phlegm— this earth that contains the five seats of phlegm.
The power possesses the five types of bile. || 829 ||
May the power that possesses the five bile-like qualities, by whose flames the mercury and other substances undergo various colors, be the remover of our bilious ailments. (29)
The awakener of the five stages. || 830 ||
She who generates awakening from non-awakening, the sole witness of all states of being,
dwelling in the single station of the heart, she awakens the five stations.
A woman in her courses. || 831 ||
Having gone before the Destroyer of Māra and having deluded him,
he deposited his own [treasure] within himself after it had been churned;
and there was the departure of Ariṣṭa and the birth of the Kumāra.
May Udakyā, satisfied by Nanda, be victorious! 31.
Desiring a male [lover] || 832 ||
If she were not a woman of supreme strength who desired the bull [Śiva], how could she have carried away the mind of the one whose seed is fire in an instant? (32)
If there is an external discharge [of semen], [the penance lasts] for three days. || 833 ||
During her menses, even though she is pure, she quickly assumes impurity;
this woman, who flows externally, remains so for three days at her own appointed time.
The power (śakti) is that which sustains the rajas and the semen. || 834 ||
May that Power, who alone restrains the all-pervading soul from every side while bearing both passion and semen, grant us the power of power. (34)
The placenta. || 835 ||

May that which carries within itself, like a seed, a tree whose body is vast though its soil is small—the world—whether it be with or without a membrane, bestow immediately and abundantly an inexhaustible and dense [result]. 35.
The one who bears the embryo. || 736 ||
By whom this fourfold creation has been manifested—whose womb could that extraordinary woman not be honored? (36)
The knower of the three times. || 837 ||
Since the three times shine forth right now before her,
victorious is this Tridevī, whose consciousness is time and who knows the three times.
It possesses three genders. || 838 ||
When the distinct manifestation of words that have coalesced together is understood as being mutually identical, may this [work], which possesses the three genders, be victorious. (38)
The triple-formed one. || 839 ||
May that protector of the mind, who possesses the three forms and by whom even a person in states such as waking or childhood becomes as if another, be victorious for me. (39)
The dweller in Tripura. || 840 ||
She by whose grace one becomes a lord of speech, desire, and power through the recitation of the syllables of speech, desire, and power—she is this Tripuravāsinī. 40.
Free from passion. || 841 ||

I bow to that Śivā, who, through the grace of her own sovereign freedom, rendered even the passionless Maheśāna full of passion; she who is beautiful with the rhythm and measure of her creative power. 41.
The Śiva-principle. || 842 ||
Having made existence extremely difficult to attain and having entered into its very core,
she who nevertheless remains established in her own virtuous character is considered to be the Śiva-tattva.
She is one who is passionately devoted to the reality of desire.

May she who has transcended the latent impressions of desire and the like, whose very nature is desirable, who is the beloved of the Conqueror of Desire, and who is enamored with the reality of desire, be victorious. (43)
The East. || 844 ||
Even for one surveying the world, that direction—
the quarter adorned by the strength of Indra, the enemy of Vṛtra— attains the status of being "the world" itself because of the sun that is ever-risen therein.
May the eastern direction pull away our grief from every side. || 44 ||
Downward. || 845 ||
Since even Antaka and even the Lord of the Dead (Yama) shine by depending upon her,
she is considered the "Direction of the Equal One" (Samavartinī) because of her description as being impartial.
The west. || 846 ||
May this western quarter— whose wise ones dwell in immovability and which is filled with the strength of living beings—
grant me rebirth once again in the west.
The northern direction. || 847 ||
She, by the worship of whom even Kubera—the lord of wealth, the king of kings, and friend of the mendicants—became the guardian of the northern quarter; she is thus esteemed as the North.
Of the intermediate directions. || 848 ||
From whom the purifier [Agni], the consumer of his own abode [Rudra], the lord of the *rakṣas* [Yama], the meritorious folk [the Maruts], the wind [Vāyu],
and even the fierce life-force (*prāṇa*) of people here on earth, all derive their power from Śambhu.
May [he] be for the gratification of those in the intermediate and cardinal directions. 48.
Egoism. || 849 ||
May the Goddess of gods, who possesses both innate and cultivated wisdom, and who is the sole source of the birth of the universe—she who is the threefold ego—be victorious. 49.
The [states] beginning with ego-grasping. || 850 ||
O Śāmbhavī, if you are not to be warded off by egoism, then remain forever within me with a joyful mind, as the Supreme One who dispels delusion.
p. 276) The illusion of strength. || 851 ||
Having reduced Viṣṇu to the state of a dwarf, he indeed pleased Bali—who had traversed the three worlds—and from him obtained incomparable strength. (51)
She who is fond of offerings. || 852 ||
Victorious is this Balipriyā, who established Hari, the Lord of all worlds, permanently at the entrance of Bali’s subterranean realm. 52.

Surely that goddess, who brings singular joy to the minds of the sacrificers, is like the *dhruvā* ladle itself; having repeatedly kindled the fire with the splendor of a full oblation, she shines forth.
The *sruva* ladle. || 854 ||

This ladle, worshipped with excellent mantras, shall be victorious through various oblations; it is the supreme cause of satisfaction for the host of gods whose faces are turned toward the sacrificial grass (barhis).
The *sāmidhenī* verses. || 855 ||
That Vedic Ṛk which, when recited at the beginning by those learned in the mantras, kindles the fire, is this great sovereign Sāmidhenī that brings victory. (55)
Possessing faith. || 856 ||

That worship which is performed with faith—whether it be obligatory, occasional, or for the sake of desired results—by those who know the essential meaning of the Vedas, is proclaimed as "faithful" (saśraddhā). || 56 ||
The deity of the ancestral rites (śrāddha). || 857 ||
She by whose grace even the ancestors, though beyond the range of sight, attain unsurpassed satisfaction through the *kavya* offering—she is the deity of the *śrāddha*. 57.
The mother. || 858 ||
May that Supreme Goddess, who protects and tenderly nurtures with her own milk— her merit— the child who is destitute and without a protector, protect us exceedingly.
May she who destroys the skin of the slain mother always be present. || 58 ||
Maternal grandmother. || 859 ||
May the Great Goddess, who sports upon the single expanse of the earth—the very root of the lineage of the Ahīnas—and who is the mother of the progenitor, the maternal grandmother, be victorious! 59.
Satisfaction. || 860 ||

Food, when prepared, is like a sown seed for the extraction of the fruit that is the bodily constituents; ultimately, that which one attends to is satisfaction, which removes the numbness of the limbs.
Father and mother. || 861 ||
She by whom this body, composed of the seven elements, was manifested here—that which is called the father, the formless abode—is considered to be both father and mother. (51)
Grandmother. || 862 ||
By whose power this existence—which brings such great joy—did not manifest;
she is the source of that power, whose grandmother is this Great One (Mahatī).
daughter-in-law || 863 ||
Victorious is this large-eyed daughter-in-law, whose virtuous conduct makes her noble family fruitful and stainless; she possesses slender limbs and great prosperity.
p. 278) Dauhitriṇī || 864 ||
She is worthy of honor by the virtuous, the cause of her family's upliftment;
by whose grace the Goddess became a mother of a daughter’s son, she is thus called "Dauhitriṇī."
Daughter || 865 ||
Therefore, that Himālaya became renowned as the Lord of Mountains, since this certain Mother of the World became his daughter in his house. (65)
A granddaughter. || 866 ||
May this granddaughter of the Supreme Sovereign, who is considered by the virtuous to be the worthy recipient of the love of her father’s son, sanctify our lineage. 66.
Naptṛī || 867 ||
May the Goddess, the Great Sovereign, who is the supreme weapon for shattering the suffering of saṃsāra and is renowned as the granddaughter [of Śiva], grant prosperity and satisfaction. 67.
Beloved of children. || 868 ||
Victorious is she who is dear to children, who exerts herself to pacify all obstacles for infants,
and who holds even the slender desires under her control.
The giver of breasts. || 869 ||
That fortunate man by whom she was worshipped with devotion as the giver of breasts would become the giver of happiness; he could not be equaled by anyone else, O lady of measured countenance. (69)
[The Murajabandha] (p.
279): The placement of these [syllables] is the Stanadhārā. || 870 ||
In this world where even the food of immortality does not bring satisfaction to living beings,
here the Mistress alone triumphs through her mere breast-milk.
The source of the universe. || 871 ||
Though he is solely born of water,
having acquired skill through compassion,
he creates the wondrous universe from all sides.
May she, the source of the universe, be made free from a womb by you.
A suckling infant. || 872 ||
How could his lineage not be supreme, vast, and stainless,
in whose house the suckling goddess is ever present?
She who holds a child in her lap. || 873 ||
May the auspicious Śivā, daughter of the mountain, be victorious— she upon whose lap the infant of the universe shines, appearing joyful and well-nourished even though he is but a child.
The swing. || 874 ||
The playful, trembling, and ever-expanding sport of the teeth, which bestows the gift of joy, has shattered the vast expanse of the world;
that playful one, who grants the gift of bliss, has indeed destroyed it.
This two-syllable [mantra] belongs to her who delights in the sport of the swing. || 875 ||
The mental fluctuation of everyone delights in that swing-play;
even she, the daughter of the Mountain, delights in that swing-play. (75)
Urvaśī || 876 ||
May she by whom the host of gods was brought under her control and went elsewhere—leaving heaven as it were—become Urvaśī for the sake of prosperity. 76.
The plantain tree. || 877 ||
Observing the similarity between her own thighs and the plantain tree in every respect, did that plantain tree itself become a destroyer of the strife of the Kali age? (77)
The cry of the peacock. || 878 ||
Who, who are the crows? The *koka*, *kaṅka*, and *kāka* crows; the *kekuka* and *kāka* crows;
the *kekāka*, *kakaka*, *aṅkoka*, *ākeka*, and *aikāka* crows—[they all] cry out "ka-ka. 78.
[The single-syllable mantra] is *viśikhā*. || 879 ||
May that Viśikhā be for your prosperity— she who, with the fire-peak brilliance of her wisdom,
purifies people from their very hair-tips with her glances.
Śikhinartinī || 880 ||
"The son who was carried by me in my womb is now being carried by him on his back;
thus, this dancer of the peacock is ever content. (80)
Alternatively,
how could the fire of the three-eyed one ever blaze without fuel,
were it not for the goddess who dances upon the flame and occupies half his body?
She who holds a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga). || 881 ||
Victorious indeed is this love of those who share a common nature:
that the wielder of the skull-topped staff, though possessing unequal eyes, finds delight in her who likewise bears the skull-topped staff. 81.
A bedstead. || 882 ||
Victorious is that certain bedstead, ever unbroken, reclining upon which the weary mendicant sleeps happily in the cemetery grounds. (82)
Following the path of the arrow's shaft.
How could the enemy of Tripura burn the three cities so swiftly by himself,
had Tripura not been his companion, following after the shaft of his arrow?
The attainment of the goal. || 884 ||

When the people of the world praise even a single lay devotee (upāsaka) excessively, this attainment of the goal— which consists of conquering [the world] a hundred thousand times— is characterized by auspicious marks.
A fraction. || 885 ||
In this Kali age, she is the essence of all arts, devoted to the playful dalliance of the *kulākulakalā*;
she is the deceptive artistry of the swarm of bees, the sweet nectar for the crow-like Kāla, and the treasury of all arts in the dark age.
(This consists of two syllables.
She is unperceivable. || 886 ||

Victorious is she who has an internal object of focus, an external object of focus, and is devoid of both the state of being an object and not being an object; she whose object of focus is the non-duality of the object and its characteristic, yet is herself beyond being focused upon or not focused upon.
It is to be characterized. || 887 ||
That which is characterized by awakening is perceived by those who know the characteristics of its parts;
though it is the very object of perception, it is one alone, being distinct from everything that is perceived.
Possessing auspicious marks. || 888 ||
For that fortunate one by whom the deity of auspicious marks is remembered moment by moment,
the mental constructions of many eons become as brief as a single instant.
...the one who abides. || 889 ||
May the Goddess, who manifests as the world, who brings about existence and non-existence, and who moves within, abide eternally within my heart. (89)
Those who practice the excellent path. || 890 ||
Why should everyone not follow that path, even if they have no desire to do so, by which Maheśvarī has always been served through the practice of the excellent way? 90.
Pervading the entire sphere of the universe, she who exists as the supreme foundation in the form of the five elements is known by the wise as the moat.
May this auspicious mine, which satisfies the learned in seven ways, destroys poverty,
and is the cause of the difficulty of attaining liberation from the miserable states of existence, be ever victorious.
Commentary: || 893 ||
Even if sprinkled by clouds and even if split open by wind and sun, how could trees flourish if there were no protective fence? (93)
Encircled by a wall. || 894 ||
By what various means do you, O Goddess who are like a surrounding wall, shine forth with your own compassion to destroy the afflictions of living beings? (94)
The Tide || 895 ||
The shore, with its essence of nectar being gathered, was pure with creepers swaying to the rhythm of the *lāmatāla* beat;
it was filled with delight, possessing the intense flow of passion, and was slow with the grace of trees and creeping vines.
This is the Sarvatobhadra; its ritual placement (nyāsa) is as follows: Ve.
Lā-rasā (The Taste of Gold)

O Mother!

They are those very ones.

come hither!

Sāra-lā.
And the boundary is in the great ocean. (896)
Victorious is that one Goddess alone, who, by her grace, allows water and land to be distinguished even within the great ocean; she is the very boundary itself. 96.
The power of nourishment. || 897 ||
Victorious is this very power of innate nature, the nourishing energy by which even the wise regard the apparatus of imperial sovereignty as a mere blade of grass. (97)
The power of desiccation. || 898 ||
Having propitiated her, even the ocean born from a jar—though deep and very vast—was dried up in an instant;
therefore, she is known as the Power of Drying (Śoṣaṇī). 98.
Long-haired woman. || 899 ||
May the auspicious one with long creeper-like eyebrows, a long face, and long eyes—she of beautiful long hair—remain well-served before me for a long time. (99)
Sulomaśā || 900 ||
Since her six virtues reside as if in great confinement within the space of her heart, they have emerged outward under the guise of body hair; such is the power of this woman with beautiful hair.
He who, by the power of his own sovereign freedom and supreme experience, has necessarily arisen in the renowned position known as Sāhib Kaula,
and who fashions a seat for himself with various poetic compositions that illuminate his form— a state unattainable by others— [is the one here].
In his poem titled *Vilāsa*, devotion reached its culmination on the fourteenth day.
Thus ends the fourteenth devotion in the *Nāmavilāsa*, composed by the illustrious and preeminent teacher of Mahāmāheśvara, Sahib Kaulānandanātha. 14.
The fifteenth devotion is Lalitā. || 901 ||
She who is celebrated as Tārā, the lineage of the world, the graceful and expansive one;
she who is embraced by her father, free from duality, and firmly established in the heart. || 1 ||
(This is a *padmabandha* [lotus-arrangement];
it is full-bodied. || 902 ||

O friend, when she, having passed through the three worlds, emerges from Śambhu, she does so with the splendors of the flood of her singular beauty— splendors that are intense as if situated in a very narrow space.
This deity is superior to the body; she is made of flesh. || 2 ||
Slender. || 903 ||

Devotees meditate upon the Mother of the Three Worlds, the daughter of the Lord of Mountains, within their minds even while they are moving; yet she is considered a slender maiden—this is truly marvelous.
She who upholds the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas. || 904 ||
Free from the state of the known and the knower, she who flashes within the mind of those who realize the unity of the five traditions is the upholder of the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas. || 4 ||
Intoxicated by drinking human blood. || 905 ||
Occupying the great realm of the Saṃkhya spirits while herself free from all mental constructs,
the consort of the Lord of Īśāna triumphs, intoxicated by the drinking of human blood.
Adorned with ornaments of human skulls and bones.
Having perceived her husband’s shame regarding his bone ornaments, did she, though possessing costly jewels, become one whose ornaments are human skulls and bones? (6)
Delight in playing with dice. || 907 ||
Deluded by her, even he who was the son of Satī and a lover of Hari lost his own sovereignty; Śivā took delight in this as if it were a mere game.
The bodily [suffering]. || 908 ||
Victory comes through a beneficial throw, and defeat through one that is not beneficial;
she who wins is the dice-board upon which the distinction between the essential and the non-essential is discerned.
The śārikā bird speaks like a parrot. || 909 ||
Śambhu was diverted from his meditative absorption by her as she cooed sweetly; she, who spoke like a parrot, was indeed that very śārikā bird, the enemy of the bodiless god of love (Anaṅga).
Śāmbarī || 910 ||

The bodiless Intellect, which for a moment and then another moment manifests both duality and unity— externally as well as internally— is a magical web of illusions that spreads out duality within unity and unity even within duality.
May that Śāmbarī, who removes delusion, ever be present. || 10 ||
The Gāruḍī Vidyā. || 911 ||
If the perfected Gāruḍī-vidyā draws from afar the wondrous host of serpents emaciated by great poison, then there shall be no fear again.
Vāruṇī || 912 ||
May that auspicious Goddess Vāruṇī be victorious, by whose grace even the dull-witted Pracetas Jaḍarāja restrains the exceedingly haughty Lord of Beings (Sattveśa).
Worshipped by Varuṇa. || 913 ||
May she who is eternally adorned with garlands of lotuses, who is incomparable in every single lotus,
who is praised by the Lord of Lotuses (Brahmā), and who is worshipped by Varuṇa, abide within the lotus.
Vārāhī || 914 ||
Having propitiated her, the supportless Kola (Boar) raised up the earth submerged in water; that Vārāhī destroys all sin. 14.
Holding a shaven head in her hand. || 915 ||
May she who runs toward the Daitya elephant as it turns away in fear, holding a severed head in her hand, protect me in this perilous battle. 15.
She who lifted up the earth with her fangs.
You alone were the boar who lifted the earth with your tusks;
otherwise, O Śivā, how could that lowest of beings, a mere boar, have lifted it?
She who assumes the form of a fish. || 917 ||
She by whom the lords of the gods and sages, containing the seeds of all living beings, are sustained at the time of dissolution, is considered to be she who bears the form of a fish.
Embodied. || 918 ||
For the sake of creation, preservation, and likewise destruction, she appeared as the embodied power of the Lord; though formless, she manifested as a form that bestows incomparable strength.
Generous. || 919 ||
Having attained which, this hollow bubble of existence would no longer come within the path of your vision; grant that [state] to me,
who am free from desire for my own desires.
Who is more generous than Yayāti? Who else besides you is so? || 19 ||
It has the image as its support. || 920 ||
You are the sovereign, a treasure-house of compassion; though you are eternally new, you have made even the insentient extremely soft for their sake.
You are the refuge of all, yet yourself without any support.
O Goddess, you are truly present even though you abide within an image. || 20 ||
It is formless. || 921 ||
The beloved of the Eightfold Form (Aṣṭamūrti), who is meditated upon even by the Tenfold Form (Daśamūrti) as his eternally uncreated singular form,
[bestows] the manifestation of that formless state consisting of consciousness and bliss.
May she grant us the removal of deceit. || 21 ||
She is the form of the treasure. || 922 ||
May she, who is the embodiment of the treasure, grant us the treasure of unconditional injunction;
and may she always establish her presence within the space of our hearts. 22.
The Śāligrāma stone is pure. || 923 ||
By what means can that pure Śyāmā-Śāligrāma stone be measured, wherein the pure-being Kṛṣṇa, Hari, became red for a moment? (23)
Mindfulness. || 924 ||
The Veda, which is infinite and unfathomable, is celebrated as fourfold with its fourfold meanings,
having been revealed by the lords of sages who were under its influence.
May mindfulness grant me that mindfulness which reaches its state. || 24 ||
It has the nature of conditioned formations. || 925 ||
Words are analyzed through phonemes and words, and the sentence is determined by those [phonemes] that have reached their finality through compassion;
it is devoid of the false nature of the form of *sphoṭa*.
May he bestow his own nature upon the form of the conditioned phenomena. || 25 ||
p. 290) Well-refined. || 926 ||
How could he not be the expresser of many [meanings], in whose heart the well-refined impressions (saṃskāras) of both past and present are spontaneously established? (26)
Cultivation || 927 ||
By whom the Vedas awaken the gods here,
and by whom the gods are made joyful for their devotees—
she is the presiding deity of the Vidyādharas.
May our refined speech proceed from the tip of the tongue. || 27 ||
The Prakrit [language]. || 928 ||
Having manifested that extraordinary power which the serpent king Piṅgala, with his many tongues, had kept hidden,
he ascended to the pure pinnacle of eloquence.
Let those be the common styles of dramatic composition. || 28 ||
The local dialect. || 929 ||
Through manifold words, the Sovereign of All expresses a single meaning everywhere;
may she who is defined by the form of the Mātṛkā grant the understanding of even the most meager local dialects. (29)
Verse 930.
O Lord, you who are praised by the three feet and also by the six auspicious ones;
O you whose forms are manifold, such as "Thā-thā," fulfill our state of seeking refuge.
A song (gīti). || 931 ||

That which, upon being heard, causes both the dull-witted and the wise here to realize a single truth and leaves them powerless even as they possess self-mastery—that alone is called "Gīti" (Song). 31.
p. 291) A riddle || 932 ||
That which acts joyfully in assemblies to break the mouths of disputants,
and which delights the wise— let one bestow such a riddle (prahelikā) here with ease.
In that part where flows the moon, an ocean of the nectar of intense bliss—oh, may the playful Bindu and Iḍā quickly remove the affliction caused by the moon! 33.
Piṅgalā || 934 ||
May the wondrous Piṅgalā, who flows through the portion where the Sun moves— she who is beautiful, whose majesty is known by the wise, and who is as marvelous as a citron— protect me from the right.
This [river], with the sweet humming of swarms of bees upon the stage of the waves of the Gaṅgā,
and with Śaṅkara embraced by Piṅgalī, would bestow a sign among the three Liṅgas.
Suṣumṇā || 936 ||
This Jyeṣṭhā, who bestows the highest and the lowest states upon the virtuous, has the nature of Agni and Soma;
she is both void and non-void through awakening, the Suṣumṇā, beginningless and endless.
The Sun-bearing River. || 937 ||

That which fills [the body] through the left, performs internal retention (kumbhaka), and is exhaled through the other, is the "sun-coursing" [channel]; it does not lead one across the stream of worldly existence.
Śaśisravā || 938 ||
By means of that which binds the solar orb, the Goddess is brought under control;
one who does not suffer from the moon's flow shall not be afflicted by old age, death, and the like. || 38 ||
Located in the palate. || 939 ||
All pervasive consciousness shines forth, established in the palate alone, just as a king, the sovereign of all the earth, resides within his own capital city. (39)
Kākinī || 940 ||
May Kākinī alone, her body made perceptible by the intoxication of tasting the supreme nectar, always be my companion. 40.
Amṛtajīvinī (The one who lives by nectar). || 941 ||
What would be accomplished by food if the one who lives on nectar were pleased? What would be accomplished by food if the one who lives on nectar were angry? (41)
Appropriate. || 942 ||
To whom would the Great Goddess not be a source of wonder, she who, though possessing a subtle form, remains pervading the entire universe as the immovable daughter of the Mountain? 42.
Of vast form. || 943 ||
Victorious are those of vast form who, residing within the atoms of the mind, are themselves conceived as the vast forms of Virāj by both sentient and insentient beings. (43)
Of light form. || 944 ||
When this triple world becomes as light as a single atom, he by whom that wondrous state is meditated upon shall never again be subject to the condition of lightness here.
Gurusthirā || 945 ||
How could he by whom she, the firm Guru, was contemplated with a steady mind, not become for a moment the eternal Guru of gurus? 45.
p. 293) Sthāvarā || 946 ||
As if out of affection for her father Sthāvareśa, that Sthāvarā herself has become a stable form; may she steady our minds. (46)
The mobile one. || 947 ||
It is wonderful that you, O daughter of the Lord of Mountains, are mobile;
yet how much more wonderful is it than anything else that you have become mobile through meditation! 47.
The Goddess || 948 ||
In play, in the desire for victory, in legal proceedings, in gambling, in praise, and even in movement, the supreme Goddess alone shines forth in her absolute sovereignty. (48)
She bestows the fruits of performed actions.
What is surprising about you, who bestow the fruits of actions performed by those who act?
But it is truly surprising that you bestow the fruits of actions performed even by those who are free from action. (49)
Her body is overwhelmed by sense objects. || 950 ||
If you, Pārvatī, were not one whose body was overcome by sensory objects, then how could you have taken refuge in Hara, the solitary skull-bearer and lord of the mountains? (50)
Without distinction. || 951 ||
Even toward the six-faced one who has the face of an elephant, Śivā— being without distinction due to the cause of her affection for him as a son— is naturally victorious through all her excellence.
Those who have conquered their senses. || 952 ||
The young woman, the treasury of all fortune, departed from her father’s house;
having conquered her senses, she came for the sake of supreme asceticism, which yields the fruit of the Great Lord.
Viśvarūpā || 953 ||

Victorious is that certain Supreme One, whose nature is consciousness, from whom the entire world of beings arises, in whom it dissolves, and of whose essence it consists; she who is the universal form. (53)
Consciousness-bliss || 954 ||
For that wise man by whom this Sundarī, who is consciousness and bliss, has been known, even Indirā, the consort of Indra, is utterly barren for the delighting of his heart.
The awakener of the Supreme Brahman. || 955 ||

It is the purifier of the darkness of delusion, the reconciler of the opposition between duality and non-duality, the obstructer of all worldly desires, and the awakener to the Supreme Brahman. || 55 ||
Unchanging. || 956 ||
Having created the universe from all sides as a flood of various forms and transformations,
she remains there alone, certain and changeless, having established herself within it.
Free from enmity. || 957 ||
Though Gaṅgā has a rival, though the moon is crooked and base, and though she dwells upon the head of her husband, the Sovereign Goddess remains free from enmity; may she be victorious! (57)
Abstention. || 958 ||
When one, though possessed of a son, a wife of like nature, a home, friends, and kinsmen,
finds no delight in them at the end, that indeed is true detachment.
The increaser of truth. || 959 ||
O Supreme Goddess, in this Kali age, which is turbid with blemish, ill-fated, and incomparable, may she be the increaser of truth for all people. (59)
The command of the Puruṣa. || 960 ||
If it is true that the command of the Great Goddess is inviolable,
may she remain steadfast for us in the shattering of ignorance and in the adorning of knowledge.
Divided. || 961 ||

Inhering in the nature of reality, she who is Śivā is victorious as she turns toward worldly existence; yet even while inhering in the nature of reality, she who is non-different from it is victorious as she turns toward worldly existence. (61)
Patience bestows absolute liberation.
The ocean of the mind agitates people with its flood of waves only so long as this patience, which bestows absolute liberation, has not been resorted to with devotion. 62.
Dwelling in solitude. || 963 ||
O Great Goddess, grant me your own state, which dwells in solitude,
so that even though I am present everywhere, I may never again perceive the world as real.
The mother who gives birth to wisdom. || 964 ||
Victorious is this auspicious Maheśvarī, who is Śivā herself, the cause of knowledge for the ignorant; she is both supreme and non-supreme, the eternal progenitor of wisdom.
One who is learned in the scriptures. || 965 ||
To whom would this Great Sovereign, so rich in sacred learning, not cause wonder—she who is of many colors in one respect, yet in another respect possesses but a single color? 65.
Devoid of activity. || 966 ||
By what means is the Supreme Goddess, who is free from desire, measured by the wise?
She by whom everything is ordained, yet nothing at all is ordained. (66)
The whole is one. || 967 ||
Victorious is she, the one who is the totality of all things, who appears as the world through her manifested form to those who do not know her, and in her true nature to those who do. 67.
She is served by all the world alone. || 968 ||
May the Sovereign Goddess, who is served by all the world, be victorious through one-pointed devotion for the attainment of the fruits of the four aims of life, according to one's desire. 68.
Service. || 969 ||
By those who have destroyed their pride and are free from sloth, this [practice] should be cultivated according to their inclination;
service performed with ever-increasing intensity at the proper time yields fruit. 69.
She is fond of service. || 970 ||
In whatever direction, place, action, or time she is worshipped accordingly,
this auspicious Goddess, who delights in service, bestows fruit in that very manner.
It should be served. || 971 ||

Having realized which [state], all supernatural powers (siddhis) become as mere blades of grass to the virtuous, that alone should be cultivated with one's whole being; how could anything else here [in this world] ever be so? 71.
It increases the fruit of service. || 972 ||
How indeed could the best of men not serve the lotus feet of him with whom Śivā is pleased—she who truly increases the fruits of service? (72)
In the Kali age, Kālī is beloved by Kalki.
How can a single young Brahmin subdue many wicked Mlecchas?
[This is impossible] when Kālī, who is dear to Kalki, is not worshipped during the Kali age. (53)
The destroyer of wicked mlecchas. || 974 ||
In former times, having brought forth Mlecchas in the form of Surabhi, she then,
in the form of Kālī, became the destroyer of those wicked Mlecchas.
The opposite. || 975 ||
Having been made into an ear-ornament by Bāṇa in an instant through his skill, the bowstring, being fully satisfied, surely brings about the attainment of the target. (75)
A staff-like bow. || 976 ||
Victorious is this bow-staff held in the hands of archers;
by means of it, those various heroes, having slain their enemies, became lords of the earth. (76)
The edge of a sword. || 977 ||
She alone, who bestows victory upon those who strike and celestial residence upon those who are slain, is the benefactor of all through the edge of the sword. (77)
Difficult to bend. || 978 ||

He in whose heart she, who is difficult to propitiate, dwells, being fully satisfied by his devotion—to him bow those who are themselves hard to bend, and even the most excellent of the gods who are worthy of worship. (78)
The horse-leap. || 979 ||
That horse-leaping, which was previously well-practiced by the groom while riding in a carriage, may it now produce great wonder and lead to abundant prosperity. (79)
The bridle. || 980 ||

That [movement] by which horses, having been repeatedly brought under control, are urged in circular paths during a race for victory, and which causes them to gallop in leaps, is considered *valgita*. (80)
May this goad, which subdues even a mad elephant through its subtle touch, be free from cruelty.
The intoxicated elephant. || 982 ||
How could that army not instantly delight the enemy’s elephants, when its vanguard is the goddess known as Sanmattavāraṇā? (82)
Born of a hero. || 983 ||
From whom the heroes have manifested, in whom they abide, and who consists of them—Vīrabhū, the supreme ground of rest, is honored upon earth. (83)
The mother of heroes. || 984 ||
Blessed is that unique Mother of Heroes, the supreme goddess who is a cow of plenty;
she protects her fallen heroes, filled with a love that knows no cause. (84)
A mother of heroes. || 985 ||
She who, like a mirror among objects made of iron, reveals her own face to those who behold it, and who gives birth to heroes among men—she is praised as a certain "Vīrasū" (mother of heroes). 85.
The daughter of Vīra. || 986 ||

She who is the daughter of the Hero (Vīranandinī) is she through whose immersion into Śambhu—the performer of the five acts—his devotees become perfectly blissful and abandon the fear of the five elements (pañcatva). 86.
Victory to Śrī! || 987 ||
May that very Goddess of Victory, who alone spreads a certain bliss consisting of the majesty of oneness with Brahman, be ever present near us from all sides. 87.
p. 299) The Jayadīkṣā initiation. || 988 ||

Having offered their enemies as sacrificial animals into the fire of their own prowess by means of the mantras of weapons, the people initiated therein shine forth; that is the auspicious initiation of victory.
The giver of victory. || 989 ||
May that Jayā, the companion of Vijayā, be forever victorious and grant us victory,
so that our state of being Dhanañjaya may manifest as something natural.
Jayavardhinī || 990 ||
What could be difficult to accomplish for one who possesses immediate clarity, if truth were always present as an ally that increases victory? (90)
Her form is graced with the beauty of good fortune. || 991 ||
May she, whose form is blessed with supreme fortune, always stand before me—she who renders the mind, even when directed toward worldly objects, steady and motionless. (91)
The increaser of all good fortune. || 992 ||
May she, by whose grace the state of Śarva comes to everyone in an instant, always be our companion, increasing all prosperity. (92)
Kṣemaṅkarī || 993 ||
Exhausted again and again by delusion, and worn out again and again by vain anxiety,
I have today suddenly become a partaker of happiness, now that Kṣemaṅkarī has been seen.
The form of accomplishment. || 994 ||
She is undoubtedly celebrated as the very form of accomplishment (siddhi) in her own nature within me;
otherwise, how could I be the Lord of all accomplishments through the perfection of my own self? (94)
p. 300) Satkīrti || 995 ||
May our excellent fame, ever radiant, be beloved by all, everywhere, at all times, and in every way—by which [fame] birth itself may truly be considered as having been born. 95.
The deity of the path. || 996 ||
May Mṛḍānī protect the person firmly mounted on an elephant, a chariot, or a horse, whether walking or always [stationary], as the deity of the path. 96.
The form consists of all sacred fords.
Through the awakening of all sacred fords (tīrtha), he is a true seeker here, like a ford itself;
for within him, the form consisting of all sacred fords brings about its own manifestation.
The radiance consists of all the gods.
For even the Ādityas and other gods are never able to dispel that darkness;
yet this radiance, composed of all the gods, can cause even that to set.
The Śakti is the bestower of all accomplishments. || 999 ||
She who is neither dispassionate nor passionate, who is devoted yet possesses an unattached mind—may this Śakti, the bestower of all perfections, be victorious, ever victorious! 99.
She who is the auspiciousness among all that is auspicious. || 1000 ||

We are blessed, we have accomplished our purpose, we are worthy of worship, and we possess all auspiciousness, since she who is the auspiciousness of all auspicious things is always known everywhere. 100.

She who causes the pure arising of the arts through the fourfold description of emotional states, which are made radiant by the dance of various honors and made to reel by the excellent flavor of wine;
she who sports in the sovereignty over those respective [arts] with celebrated grace.
This is the supreme power; O Śrī, conquer all through you, the auspiciousness of all that is auspicious. || 101 ||

p. 301) He who, by means of the power that brings about the manifestation of his own absolute freedom, necessarily established himself in the station renowned as Sāhibkaula and fashioned a seat for himself—
his poetic work, concerning a subject beyond the reach of ordinary thought, contains such compositions as the *satpadmabandha* and others.
In the [work] named *Devīnāmavilāsa*, the devotion to the Goddess is marked by divisions according to the lunar days (*tithi*).
Thus ends the fifteenth devotion in the *Nāmavilāsa*, composed by the eminent teacher of the Great Maheśvara, Sāhib Kaulānandanātha. 15.
Thus, through his own power, Śiva proclaimed the sixteenth devotion to the new Lord, who possesses pure awareness of being.
Then, who indeed would not bow down to him, whose very form has been made the object of my observation? 1.
Having obtained permission with devotion from the venerable Lord of Teachers, who is the supreme experience,
one should recite [this] while inwardly concentrating and restraining the external.
And the pure one [perceives] the multitude of the senses in all three ways as well. || 2 ||
Being proficient in the authority over the mantras taught in the Tantras, disciplined, faithful, and a sole abode of exalted joy, he should perform [the rite] twice, thrice, or once in the morning.
And meditating upon it, he should recite it at the three junctions of the day.
Seated before the reciter of praises, with a concentrated mind and great joy, one should listen with palms joined in reverence after bowing down. (p. 303)
Or one should cause this king of hymns to be heard.
That which, having agitated the inner mind, strives even out of fear of excessive burden to cast off the body—
that threefold form, though nourished, [remains] despite effort.
Even in a dream, suffering shall not touch him.
Even when one desires to obtain [a better state] through the loss of country and so forth, and does not consider [the current state] to be defiled,
such a person still adopts the mode of life of beasts.
There will be an abundance of wealth and grain without effort. || 6 ||
Having disregarded even those who are renowned as invincible when their wealth is amassed, and others who are subject to their power, he wanders unobserved.
That splendor, too, would be dependent [on something else]. || 7 ||
Alone and without any retinue, he disregards even those things gathered for his sake;
being satisfied with what he has attained, he performs the activities he desires.
That would necessarily be a powerful state of strength. || 8 ||
When heroes, having raised their own prowess,
resort through yoga and other means to that exceedingly rare status established by Śauri— this [is the case].
How could such splendor not be free from theft? || 9 ||
When a patient, though wise, has fallen into a mistaken understanding regarding physicians and the like, what will he not do? How great indeed is the loss for him from that disease!
Even that grief, which has its origin in this, is far away.
Even the Moon and the Sun, though greedy for it,
strive individually to ascend the path that rises high above them throughout the day and night.
And may that fame and majesty both be under your control. || 11 ||
That blessedness, which even the wealthy find exhausting to attain, and by which the poor become no longer wretched—
that blessedness consists of the lineage, name, and conduct.
But how could it not be dependent upon perception and the other [means of knowledge]? || 12 ||

Desire and the other passions, by a mere fraction of their power, constantly agitate even those whose desires are already fulfilled and who tremble with apprehension at the prospect of attaining even through their good fortunes— those very objects of desire.
Would one not be fortunate enough to partake in this auspiciousness? || 13 ||
How great indeed is that state of being honored by the world, since even here he shines like a king without a kingdom among those who partake in assemblies of the venerable!
Even the state of being worshipped by Lokeśvara has been abandoned. || 14 ||

What person does that perfection of form—not merely remembered, but actually seen—fail to render a state of swoon? How much more so, then, would it be [effective] when present? (p. 305) How could it be otherwise?
Just as the limbs do not correspond to the limbs [of the body] according to their actual meaning. 15.
Deprived of which qualities one does not attain excellence,
and by which one shines at the end like a beast;
these are not [attained] through the praise and grace of the Guṇa-less One.
How could those various qualities ever be contained within words? || 16 ||
For even the celebrated and radiant Pūṣan, as well as his shadow, possess beauty only by virtue of their dependence upon him;
he alone brings about the stability of the world.
How is it that even that radiance does not illuminate? 17.
Heroes do not waver even when engaged in cruel deeds upon the battlefield, for they are serene;
that infinite fortitude is what is extolled by the noble ones.
Vigor is not for the sake of attaining the status of a lord of heroes. || 18 ||
What blessings are there in this world that do not lead to one's welfare, even for their mere maintenance,
each of which depends entirely upon oneself?
They become further increasers. || 19 ||
Even Viṣṇu, having beheld her who is ever-fickle, is never able to create another like her;
she is the source of auspiciousness, filled with perfected being, and honored by all.
That Śrī herself, being enamored, shall serve him. || 20 ||
Those by whom one is threatened experience suffering here,
and being deprived of autonomy, they go to hell in the next world;
why do all such things not become insignificant?
Even during sleep, sins do not attain the state of non-existence. || 21 ||
Having conquered each successive opponent in order to intimidate those in other vehicles,
this one who abides in the arising of compassion cannot be overcome by anyone else.
Those others, such as greed and the rest, would likewise be further [subdivisions]. || 22 ||
That which shines here within like a king,
with whom even Death becomes a source of fear when joined together, and who shine as their own distinct bodies— [all these are but reflections].
Do kinsmen not lead to internal bondage? || 23 ||
These daughters, who have grown up among others as if they were diseased— by whom the family falls into a state of servitude— are [yet] the lineage [itself] through their status as sons.
If they were merely striking, how could they lead to happiness? || 24 ||
How could those renowned as co-practitioners of dharma not be impassioned, when they delight one another,
adorned with ornaments and ever virtuous?
His wives were noble, possessed of both passion and youth. || 25 ||

Those who are the causes for destroying the fear of malevolent names, whose speech—like a flood of nectar even in childhood—is renowned for its noble qualities in upholding the lineage; (p. 307) those [who possess such virtues]...
Let these excellent sons perform the adornment sufficiently. || 26 ||
By seeing which,
one easily crosses over the thorny obstacle of doubt regarding the continuity [of the lineage] and attains rest, with all burdens cast aside— just as you have.
May the grandsons extend their purifying conduct.
Those who, born of great merit, have accumulated [virtue] throughout their entire lives and are thus preeminent,
[fill] the temple with great festivals— [the temple] of Indira alone...
One should always fear dwelling with these. || 28 ||
Always free from discord in their duties, they are devoted with affection and speak words that are beneficial and truthful;
they eliminate mental distraction and have transcended—
Even those who are full of suspicion will serve him if he has good servants. || 29 ||
In these primary sciences, which are heart-pleasing, composed of faultless verse and prose, intoxicating with the joy of wine, and instantly producing clarity of mind—
The rule for the initial and final [elements] shall apply starting from the first letter. || 30 ||
Foremost among those whose wealth is incalculable skill, the sacrificer, having obtained through merit that which is attainable by mere remembrance,
takes up the Lord of Praise and lauds him.
Entering into battle, how could he not be victorious? || 31 ||
And whatever object he offers for purchase or sale out of his own self-confidence,
by that very thing, by that very thing, he does not possess abundant wealth.
How indeed could a Vaiśya be one whose wealth is easily acquired? || 32 ||
Just as even one of another caste, by serving with effort, does not attain full happiness like a Śūdra,
so too it is only when one is favored by the Lord through praise that [one attains it].
What indeed does he not attain when his efforts have been cast aside? || 33 ||
They are the lords of those who desire sons among those possessing sons,
and they fulfill the abundance of wealth for those desiring wealth; whatever object of desire one fixes upon in the mind, [they grant it].
That seeker of desire attains his wish to his heart's content; he is not far from this.
One should pursue that very path by which there may be happiness here or in the next world,
even if it is attained only through great exertion;
one should not turn toward unrighteousness.
If it were to exist beforehand, would it not simply be that very dharma? || 35 ||
With her form she surpasses even Rati, and with her character she increases the aspirations of even Satī;
she acts as the sole cause of joy.
In that context, the word *kanyā* also carries the sense of "daughter. || 36 ||
The fields shall flourish with crops, free from various obstacles,
and the cows shall yield even more milk.
Just as rivers are wish-fulfilling cows that yield water from their jars. || 37 ||
Whatever is obstructed by something else so that it cannot perform any function is never truly non-existent;
for even that which displays its splendor through the fullness of its qualities remains concealed.
How could those calamities exist by which he has been struck down? || 38 ||
There shall be no fear from the king, nor from one who has gained power, nor from an enemy, nor even from wicked arts;
whether in auspicious or in inauspicious matters.
His intention shall always be auspicious. || 39 ||
She who gratifies her own circle of kinsmen with gifts, honor, and hospitality,
and by means of the acquisition of fame and her celebrated name.
He shall attain the state of being a true leader of his lineage. || 40 ||
Just as the planets, though closely attached and resting within their orbits, do not touch the sky, so too,
upon hearing the name of Rāma, they would not [touch him].
Even the Rākṣasas are not able to even look upon him. || 41 ||
Upon seeing that son of Vinatā, the Kākodaras (serpents) would become as if devoid of passion from afar;
yet, they have sought refuge in him with affection, as if in Mahādeva.
Even spirits and piśācas would attend upon him. || 42 ||
The *ḍākinīs* and mothers should protect him thoroughly, as if with affection for their own son;
and wild animals [should treat] one whose strength has been utterly destroyed...
Just as [beasts] would flee upon seeing a five-faced lion. || 43 ||
Those who are unable to produce either pleasure or pain are nonetheless inevitably tormented by the seizing spirits that have gripped the children in fear.
Why would they not be yours through his grace? || 44 ||
Those pairs of opposites here which never reach a reconciliation, or those which were previously united but have once again become characterized by affection and hatred;
Why is it not well known that this brings about joy for him? || 45 ||
Though bound by heavy chains in a difficult prison cell and repeatedly struck for his offense,
[the king] was [liberated] through the meditation and other [virtues] of this great-souled one.
How might he not be released, as one who is already liberated here? || 46 ||
He did not experience grief arising from his own son like Rāma,
nor from his own kinsmen like Vasiṣṭha or Acyuta, nor grief caused by an enemy like the Ten-faced one.
And he who lives for an eon would witness their separation.
Even the blind may obtain the strength of an eagle reaching into the eyes, just as the world of living beings receives light from the sun;
one overcome by deafness shall quickly become possessed of hearing.
Even though mute, he was like a parrot through his mastery of speech. || 48 ||
Just as an embryo is stabilized by the supreme mudrā through the seminal drop (*bindu*) within the womb,
would it not remain stable even while falling? This state of having a bound embryo persists even during emission.
And an easy delivery is certainly not difficult to obtain. || 49 ||
By means of this new [recitation] of the Sūrya[-sūkta], having attained a divine body like that of a peacock through the ever-new [practice],
one is freed from misfortune by reciting the Śruti.
How could he not be joyful? || 50 ||
Having restrained the group of senses— which, though possessing a collection of afflictions never seen before—
is pure through the study of this Veda— this son is truly pure.
One who is established through attainment would be like Vasudeva. || 51 ||
From these ten great diseases, such as quartan fever and others,
as well as those arising from spirits and the like, [protection] shall come even by hearing [this].
Just as one is liberated by consuming the lord of the Drasa [poison]. || 52 ||
One should not forget what has been heard, nor treat what has not been heard as equal to it; one should bring even that to the level of a clear record,
and one should become a speaker like the ancient masters of speech.
Even a child may defeat the elderly with his poetic compositions.
Even a mortal who, though situated in a body of enjoyment, should recite or study the *Stava* on the fivefold path with an undistracted mind;
One would not obtain the final [result], but only this initial enjoyment.
Whether in a secret place or one well-known, the wise man, established in the Goddess, remains for nine nights near her image,
filled with devotion and deeply immersed.
He has attained a state of solitude even in his mind. || 55 ||
He who, having cast aside fear and resorted to the wisdom of fortitude, causes the Lord of Praise to revolve a hundredfold,
shall have his own desires manifest before him.
That auspicious Bhavānī is ready to bestow [her grace]. || 56 ||
[In a pair of verses: Indeed, on a beautiful mountain that is a seat of the Siddhas, a preeminent sacred field, or in the abode of the gods;
Through the practice of the portion of worldly renown, accomplishment is swiftly attained;
and through recitation, that most desired accomplishment becomes perfected.
He who, having conquered his wicked senses, remains on the ground or upon a bed or seat, should recite [the mantra] ten times,
having taken food that is either restrained or measured, with the utterance of "svāhā."
And he saw the Goddess, the Sovereign, standing upon her excellent throne in a dream.
Those best of men who recite this praise with devotion a thousand times become perfected ones,
skilled in the performance of supernatural attainments.
They should be capable of both restraint and favor. || 59 ||
Even treatises that are not mastered through repeated study may become infused with the refinement of excellent poetry; indeed,
the masters of speech [the gods] seem to speak them spontaneously.
They bear splendor and eloquence as they blossom forth. || 60 ||
Delighting those nails with the mass of various jewels from their crowns,
the Great Lords are renowned for the gift of all their possessions.
They worship him as the hosts of immortals worship Śambhu.
Having inscribed [the mantra] on birch bark with the eight-fold Śākta perfumes on an auspicious day, one should worship it, as well as nine virgins,
brahmins, and excellent women, with sandalwood and other offerings.
Having gratified them with various principal foods of ambrosia. || 62 ||
Those who bind this [mantra] around their neck, hand, or head, or in their home for the purpose of protection—
especially so for young colts— [attain success].
They shall be possessors of fame and honored by kings. || 63 ||
[In a pair:
He does not return from evil food, nor from kings, nor from their wives, nor from malevolent sorcery.
There shall be no fear of an evil rebirth, nor even of the ocean or rivers, nor even from such things as ships. || 64 ||
Whether at dice, in battle, in authority, or in dispute,
how is it that even victorious men and venerable kings do not attain victory?
Why do they not go forth as his messengers with devotion? || 65 ||
How could those women, full of youth, reeling from the awakening of passion, overwhelmed by them, and enslaved by the color of love—
not themselves fall into attachment?
Excellent women do not resort to any other arts. || 66 ||
Having drawn this [mantra] and purified himself, whoever wears it on his head or neck while standing in battle,
his enemies will not look at him even once as he fights.
Even if an enemy warrior comes before him face-to-face. || 67 ||
Or the hero who, having inscribed the Lord of Praise upon banners and other such objects, enters into the count of the syllables—
even if he beholds this single [name] in many ways.
Would the enemies not become deprived of their vigor? || 68 ||
Their consciousness lost and as bewildered as children, unable even to remember their own weapons,
they [beheld] him whose body was the very abode embraced by the Goddess of Victory.
Why would the Nārakas not go to him for refuge? || 69 ||
Wherever the Lord is depicted, whether on the body or in the home, and is fully worshipped,
there neither malevolent sorcery nor a curse can prevail.
Not even the bandits were able to inflict any harm.
Neither the pinning down by Bāṇa, Vīra, and others, nor any *kṛtyā* spell, nor *pūtanā* and the like;
neither ghosts, nor *piśācas*, nor *rākṣasas*.
Or rather, spirits never enter there at all. || 71 ||
There, no fear whatsoever shall ever arise from weapons, fire, water, or wind;
even the evils of the wicked are [subdued] there by the Buddha’s—
They would not, under any circumstances whatsoever, cause an obstacle. || 72 ||
Even in elephant stables, horse stalls,
cow pens, or enclosures for goats and other animals, one should recite this *kūṭa* with devotion for the pacification of their faults.
One should enter this new [practice] for the sake of removing disease. || 73 ||
Even the servants of Yama would not be able to look upon one who praises [him] from afar;
having enjoyed pleasures here, he goes to the world of Śiva.
After a long time, at the end, the infinite supreme state is attained.
In all terrible afflictions and in every obstruction to spiritual accomplishments, one should first perform the respective ritual for this [deity],
who is the sole auspiciousness of all and the dispeller of suffering.
One who desires heaven should recite it constantly with a concentrated mind. || 75 ||
Having fully gratified the Lord of Praise with unsurpassed offerings while he was engaged in recitation,
[the sage] stood before him, [offering] the supreme benediction.
Or one who desires all that has been heard here should listen to it. || 76 ||
This thousand names of the Primordial Goddess, which is the singular merit of merits and the source of all prosperity, was proclaimed by the Lord;
its splendor was indeed fully revealed by Nandikeśvara.
Who here would not rejoice, for he is the sole cause of manhood? || 77 ||
No other hymn has been proclaimed as more supreme than this; nor is there another mantra in the Tantra whose power is ordained, nor is there any other Vidyā.
She alone is the primordial Siddhā; no other sacred site is renowned as being so capable.
To destroy the evil one, this [mantra], which has arisen from that [source] and possesses all forms, is uttered on every side. || 78 ||
Blessed are certain individuals of celebrated fame, reckoned as the sole possessors of full merit;
they are the lords of kings throughout the three worlds, worthy of honor and possessing great dignity;
not born of another source, their delusions have been destroyed by a supreme understanding of the doctrines.
Those who worship the Primordial Power (Ādi-Śakti) along the path of supreme bliss, ascending ever higher; || 79 ||
